title: Connecting the Evidence

beats.narrativeText: Atlas lays out every recovered record, observation and experiment from the entire campaign, side by side, in a single investigation archive.
Looked at separately, several explanations for what happened at Outpost Echo still seem plausible. Only one of them, though, can actually account for every piece of evidence at once.
The learner reviews the evidence gathered across the entire campaign — seventeen missions' worth, all at once.
Organising the findings into groups starts to do something no single mission could: show how individually small discoveries fit into one coherent explanation.
The learner must identify how the discoveries actually relate to each other, and support their conclusions with evidence rather than intuition about how the story probably goes.
Weighing the alternative explanations against each other, the learner narrows everything down to a single account — the one that actually fits every piece of evidence gathered since Mission 1.
The learner reflects on just how many investigations that once felt separate — weather, water, power, geology, star charts — turn out to be part of exactly one larger story.
The complete story of Outpost Echo is finally taking shape. All that's left is confirming it — and solving the expedition mystery for good.

activities.title: Review Evidence
activities.storyContext: Atlas has assembled every recovered record, observation and experiment from the whole campaign into a single investigation archive.
activities.instructions: Review the evidence gathered throughout the campaign so far, mission by mission if that helps you keep track.

activities.title: Organise Findings
activities.storyContext: Individual discoveries that felt unrelated at the time may fit together into a single coherent explanation.
activities.instructions: Organise your findings into related groups, however you think they connect.

activities.title: Identify Relationships
activities.storyContext: Discoveries that once seemed unrelated may actually be connected — the real work is naming exactly how.
activities.instructions: Identify the relationships between your organised groups of evidence, and be specific about what links them.
activities.output: A description of the relationships between findings.

activities.title: Support Conclusions With Evidence
activities.storyContext: Only one explanation accounts for all of the available evidence — not just the pieces that are easiest to explain.
activities.instructions: Write a conclusion supported by the evidence you have connected, addressing the full picture rather than a partial one.

activities.title: Evaluate Alternative Explanations
activities.storyContext: Several plausible interpretations of the evidence remain possible — dismissing them without a reason isn't the same as ruling them out.
activities.instructions: Evaluate a couple of alternative explanations properly, and explain specifically why your conclusion fits the evidence better than they do.

activities.title: Produce an Investigation Board
activities.storyContext: A visual investigation board would help show how all the clues connect.
activities.instructions: Produce an investigation board linking the clues you've gathered visually.

activities.title: How Evidence-Based Explanations Are Built
activities.storyContext: Connecting scattered evidence into one explanation is exactly what detectives and scientists do.
activities.instructions: Find out how detectives, archaeologists and scientists build evidence-based explanations.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: Which single piece of evidence changed your understanding of the mystery the most, and what did you believe before you found it?

discussionPoints: Which piece of evidence changed your thinking the most?
Why is it useful to consider more than one explanation before deciding?
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a conclusion that accounts for the full range of evidence, not just the most memorable pieces.

completionCriteria: Evidence reviewed, findings organised, and conclusions supported with evidence.
